scope: Final course batch source audit; derived and toy examples marked separately.

claims.claim: Official benchmark docs distinguish online serving, offline throughput, forward/kernel benchmarks and other specialized evaluation modes.
The vLLM bench serve CLI accepts dataset, prompt-count, request-rate, max-concurrency and backend parameters for controlled experiments.
Request rate controls arrival pacing while max concurrency constrains simultaneously outstanding client requests.
Repeated deterministic prompts against the same server can reuse prefix cache and inflate later benchmark results.
The guide defines TTFT, ITL, TPOT and E2E at benchmark client timing boundaries; ITL may differ from request-level TPOT.
The benchmark documentation recommends GuideLLM for production serving load tests because of additional request format, dataset and load flexibility.
Success request throughput, output token throughput and failure share are computed from success/failure counts, generated tokens and elapsed time; the 30/10/20 toy numbers are not measurements.
